findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs error IDs with the wrong events
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi` (src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:174-209) removes duplicate ids, puts the uncached results first, and then appends cached hits with `items.update(cache_items)`. So `events.values()` is not in `error_ids` order once some ids are cached. It is also shorter than `error_ids` when there are duplicates. When that happens, `zip` gives an event's title, message and timestamp to a different error ID, and Seer receives the mismatched data. Nothing fails or logs. The fix is to look each one up by key: `data = events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=eid))` for each `eid` in `error_ids`.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` takes `timestamp` from the error event's nodestore payload, which is a float in seconds. `gen_request_data` compares it with the top-level `timestamp` of each replay recording event, which rrweb stores in epoch milliseconds (`event_parser.py:182` passes it into the log text unchanged). A seconds value is always smaller than a milliseconds value, so every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb. The log Seer receives then also mixes the two units in its `at {timestamp}` text. The summary is told errors happened at the start of the session, and nothing reports the problem. Convert the error timestamp to milliseconds (`* 1000`) before sorting and comparing.

findings.title: Assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check. Requests that the endpoint then rejects are still counted as assemble events, which inflates the metric. Consider moving the call after the feature check, or after the request has been validated.

findings.title: One invalid report drops the whole batch
findings.body: If any report in the array fails validation, the endpoint returns 422 and none of the valid reports in the same POST are counted. Browsers batch reports from different pages, and the endpoint accepts report types it does not control, so one malformed entry loses every report sent with it. Consider skipping and logging the invalid entries and processing the rest.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check is skipped when either value is 0
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check truthiness: `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A report with `age: 0` and a timestamp, or with `timestamp: 0` and an age, passes both checks even though it has both fields. A report with neither field also passes, because both fields are `required=False`. Consider checking `"age" in self.initial_data` instead, and requiring exactly one of the two fields in `validate()`.

findings.title: Flag-gated TableWidgetVisualization always renders empty
findings.body: With `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, every table widget renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and empty `data`. `result.data`, `result.meta` and `fields` are all ignored, so any organization with the flag sees blank tables. If this is meant as scaffolding, consider passing the real result data through before the flag is turned on for anyone.

findings.title: Attribute keys query lost retry:false / staleTime:0 / refetchOnWindowFocus:false and the environment filter
findings.body: The old `useApiQuery` call set `retry: false`, `staleTime: 0` and `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. The new `useQuery` uses none of them, so it falls back to the app's QueryClient defaults. If those defaults include retries, a failing attributes endpoint now gets retried, and `isLoading` (which is now `isFetching`) stays true longer while that happens. The query also used to send `selection.environments`; `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` leaves it out on purpose (useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:50). That means the key list no longer narrows by the selected environment. Please confirm both changes are intended. If not, add the old options back to `useQuery`.

findings.title: Custom renderer results that are falsy get replaced by the default
findings.body: Both renderers fall back to the default with `if (cell)` (lines 32 and 71). The documented contract is that only `undefined` means "use the fallback", so a custom renderer that returns `0`, `''` or `null` on purpose gets overwritten by the default cell. Check `cell !== undefined` instead.

findings.title: Story copy typo and missing spaces
findings.body: "the the most basic example" repeats "the". There is no space before `tableData` (line 28), and there are similar gaps around `TabularData` (line 58) and `renderTableBodyCell` (line 111), so the rendered text runs words together, e.g. "requirestableData".

findings.title: "Project not found" can show while projects are still loading
findings.body: `useProjectFromId` (static/app/utils/useProjectFromId.tsx:7-12) looks the id up in `useProjects().projects` and ignores the `fetching` state. Line 90 therefore shows the error alert any time the project list doesn't contain the replay's project yet. That includes the moment before the projects store has loaded, so the user sees a 'Project not found' error flash before the summary loads. Consider also reading `fetching` from `useProjects()` and showing the loading state until it finishes.

findings.title: Tests use second-based breadcrumb timestamps, so they hide a seconds-vs-milliseconds mixup when errors are interleaved
findings.body: `gen_request_data` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:153-155) compares `error_events[i]["timestamp"]` with the recording event's top-level `timestamp`. The error timestamp comes from nodestore event data (`data.get("timestamp")`, line 115), which is in epoch seconds. The top-level `timestamp` on an rrweb recording event is in epoch milliseconds. These tests use seconds for the breadcrumbs (`1.5`/`2.0` here, and `float(now.timestamp())` at lines 188 and 254), so the interleaving looks correct. With real recordings, every error timestamp is about 1000× smaller than every breadcrumb timestamp, so all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb. Their `at ...` values are then in a different unit from the breadcrumbs' values. The summary sent to Seer comes out in the wrong order, and nothing reports it. Please build the fixtures with millisecond breadcrumb timestamps, as real segments have, and convert one side in `gen_request_data` (for example, multiply the error timestamp by 1000) so the ordering assertion tests the real case.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 4.** Part 1 of 4 has two problems that need fixing, both in the new error-context code of the replay breadcrumb summary. First, `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs error IDs with the wrong nodestore events, because `get_multi` removes duplicates and puts cached hits last. Second, error timestamps in seconds are compared with rrweb timestamps in milliseconds, so every error is placed before the first breadcrumb. Neither fails or logs anything; the summary is just wrong. The rest are smaller points the author can decline: the preprod analytics event is recorded before the feature check; the browser-report collector drops the whole batch when one report is invalid, and its age/timestamp exclusion check skips values of 0; and the flag-gated table widget always renders empty. The other files are refactors or config changes, and I found nothing to flag in them.

**Batch 2 of 4.** The refactor from multi-yAxes to a single yAxis per Visualize holds up in this part. Visualize.fromJSON now returns an array, and its two callers handle that: aggregateFields.tsx flattens it, and the writable path in findAllFieldRefs switched to isBaseVisualize. The remaining notes are all "consider": useTraceItemAttributeKeys silently changed its query options (retries, staleness, and the dropped environment filter); the new table renderers treat any falsy custom result as "use the fallback"; and the story text has a typo and missing spaces. One thing outside this part: savedQueries/exploreParams.tsx:29 still reads `visualize.yAxes`, so it should be checked against the new Visualize shape.

**Batch 3 of 4.** I reviewed all 25 files in this part and found one minor issue (a "consider"). In the replay AI summary tab, the "Project not found" error can flash while the projects list is still loading, because the lookup ignores the loading state.

Checks that came back clean:
- **Flex refactors:** they keep the same layout as the styled divs they replace.
- **Explore spec updates:** they match the new API.
  - `Visualize` now takes a single y-axis, and `fromJSON` returns an array.
  - The attribute-values hook now gets its `attributeKey` and `search` from a search callback.
- **Python test updates:** they line up with the changes in the other parts of this pull request (new PR comment format, `autofix_automation_tuning` default of "off", browser report validation, removal of the regex experiment and the migration test).

This was a read-only review; I didn't run any of the tests.

**Batch 4 of 4.** Part 4 is all tests. I found one problem, in the replay breadcrumb-summary tests. The breadcrumb timestamps there are in seconds, but real recording events carry milliseconds. Error timestamps from nodestore are in seconds. So the tests hide the fact that `gen_request_data` compares values in two different units, and with real recordings every error would be listed before all breadcrumbs. I couldn't fully confirm the millisecond unit from the code I read, so this finding is medium confidence. The detector owner tests match the validator's create, update and clear logic. The delayed-workflow tests pass the new `dcg_to_slow_conditions` argument correctly. The new logs top-events test computes the counts it expects correctly. I found no problems in those files.
